what_happened: In job y179, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. This job retries an earlier attempt that was interrupted when the machine ran out of disk while recording the verifier's verdict, so the verifier's reasons were lost. The new reading did not carry over what that attempt had settled. The user restated it: keep the approach that cut the test check from about 12 to 7.8 minutes. Production changes are allowed when behavior is unchanged and each has a test. Those two changes are the secret scanner's per-process memo for identical text (crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs) and the shorter poll schedule in run_check (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs). Both are deliverables. The target is the full cargo test --locked under 7 minutes, with per-binary before and after times measured and recorded in docs/decisions.md. nextest is rejected, with its measurement (584 s vs 673 s). No test may be removed, weakened or filtered.
cause: A retry's reading is built from the request text alone. Athena keeps no record of what the interrupted attempt achieved, decided or was allowed to change, and nothing compares the new reading with that earlier state. The attempt's verdict was also lost to disk exhaustion, so even a stage that looked for prior findings would have found none. The user is therefore the only carrier of the approach, the allowed production changes, the target and the rejected alternative.
prevention: When a job is a retry or follow-up of an earlier attempt, the reading stage is given a stored summary of that attempt: the approach taken, measured results, rejected alternatives, deliverables and the allowed change scope. The reading must restate these, and a check flags any difference. The attempt's decisions are written to the job record as they are made, so a lost verdict does not lose them. Disk space is also checked before the verdict is recorded.
proposed_request: Speed up Athena's full `cargo test --locked` run to under 7 minutes, continuing the approach that already brought it from about 12 to 7.8 minutes. Production changes are allowed where behavior is unchanged and each has its own test. They are: (1) a per-process memo in the secret scanner (crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs) for identical text, and (2) a shorter poll schedule in run_check (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs). Both are deliverables. Measure per-binary test times before and after in this job, and record them in docs/decisions.md. Record that nextest was rejected, with its measurement (584 s vs 673 s). Do not remove, weaken or filter any test. Make sure there is enough free disk before the verifier records its verdict.
